answer: Give each identity a non-transferable forecasting record and let scarce contracts allocate influence by calibrated accuracy, not account count. When a farm splits one skilled predictor into many names, the new histories start empty; copying its river of old calls creates an echo that auditors can match, while independent track records require each head to make costly, testable predictions over time. A saffron-colored audit sample reveals correlated timing or identical errors, so linked heads share one capped score rather than multiplying votes.
